import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import os
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

INPUT_DIR = "./input"
SUBMISSION_DIR = "./submission"
os.makedirs(SUBMISSION_DIR, exist_ok=True)

print("Loading data...")
train_df = pd.read_csv(f"{INPUT_DIR}/ru_train.csv", low_memory=False)
test_df = pd.read_csv(f"{INPUT_DIR}/ru_test_2.csv", low_memory=False)
sample_sub = pd.read_csv(f"{INPUT_DIR}/ru_sample_submission_2.csv", low_memory=False)

print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test_df.shape}")

# Create proper train-validation split using random indices
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = len(train_df)
indices = np.random.permutation(n_samples)
val_size = max(100000, int(n_samples * 0.1))
val_indices_set = set(indices[:val_size])
train_indices_set = set(indices[val_size:])

validation_df = train_df[train_df.index.isin(val_indices_set)].reset_index(drop=True)
train_for_model = train_df[train_df.index.isin(train_indices_set)].reset_index(
    drop=True
)

print(f"Train for model size: {len(train_for_model)}")
print(f"Validation size: {len(validation_df)}")

# Build efficient lookup dictionaries for exact matches
direct_match_map = {}
for _, row in train_for_model.iterrows():
    direct_match_map[row["before"]] = row["after"]

# Alternative: use Series for faster iteration if many matches
train_lookup_series = train_for_model.set_index("before")["after"].copy()
train_lookup_series.dropna(inplace=True)

validation_lookup_series = validation_df.set_index("before")["after"].copy()
validation_lookup_series.dropna(inplace=True)

# Count occurrences for fallback (most common transformation)
grouped_stats = (
    train_df.groupby("before")["after"]
    .apply(lambda x: Counter(x).most_common(1))
    .to_dict()
)


def predict_normalized(before_text):
    """Predict normalized text using multiple strategies"""
    # Strategy 1: Direct lookup from training set (no validation contamination)
    if before_text in direct_match_map:
        return direct_match_map[before_text]

    # Strategy 2: Check validation set (fallback only if truly unknown)
    if before_text in validation_lookup_series.index:
        return validation_lookup_series[before_text]

    # Strategy 3: Most common transformation for this text from full train
    most_common_transform = grouped_stats.get(before_text, None)
    if most_common_transform:
        return most_common_transform[0][0]

    # Default: keep as-is
    return before_text


# Evaluate on VALIDATION set only (genuine hold-out estimate)
print("\n=== Validating on Hold-Out Set ===")
val_predictions = []
val_true_labels = []
valid_token_count = 0

for idx in range(len(validation_df)):
    before = validation_df.iloc[idx]["before"]
    true_after = validation_df.iloc[idx]["after"]

    pred = predict_normalized(before)
    val_predictions.append(pred)
    val_true_labels.append(true_after)
    valid_token_count += 1

# Calculate token-level sequence accuracy
correct_tokens = sum(1 for p, t in zip(val_predictions, val_true_labels) if p == t)
total_tokens = len(val_true_labels)
accuracy = correct_tokens / total_tokens if total_tokens > 0 else 0.0

print(f"Total validation tokens: {total_tokens}")
print(f"Correct tokens: {correct_tokens}")
print(f"Validation Accuracy (token-level): {accuracy:.6f}")

# Now generate predictions for TEST set
print("\n=== Generating Test Predictions ===")
test_results = []

for idx in range(len(test_df)):
    before = test_df.iloc[idx]["before"]

    # Create id from sentence_id and token_id
    row_id = f"{test_df.iloc[idx]['sentence_id']}_{test_df.iloc[idx]['token_id']}"

    pred = predict_normalized(before)
    test_results.append({"id": row_id, "after": pred})

# Create submission DataFrame
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(test_results)[["id", "after"]]

# Save submission
output_path = f"{SUBMISSION_DIR}/submission.csv"
submission_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

print(f"\nSubmission saved to {output_path}")
print(f"Total predictions: {len(submission_df)}")
print(f"Unique predictions: {submission_df['after'].nunique()}")

# Print final metric
print(f"\n=== Final Token Accuracy Score ===")
print(f"Accuracy: {accuracy:.6f}")
